advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where both endpoints of a new Blocks edge are active with empty deps, asserting exactly one edge is emitted (or document that a redundant inverse emit is harmless/idempotent at apply time).
evidence: inbound_differ.py:530-532: guard only fires `if (inverse, this_id) in ld.deps_as_set(counterpart)` — i.e. only when the counterpart's deps ALREADY contain the edge
mutations are not applied to the in-memory ticket dicts during a pass, so when both X and Y are iterated in the same compute_inbound_mutations call neither counterpart yet owns the edge
test_link_direction_absolute.py `test_genuine_new_jira_link_is_adopted` passes `_OUTWARD_BLOCK` for X only; there is no test with both endpoints' issuelinks present and empty deps on both
advisory.finding: For a genuinely-new blocking edge between two ACTIVE tickets where neither yet carries the local dep, both endpoints emit their side in the same pass (X emits `blocks->Y`; Y emits `depends_on->X`) because the inverse-aware guard only suppresses when the counterpart ALREADY owns the inverse edge. This double-emit path is not covered by the new tests (test_genuine_new_jira_link_is_adopted uses a single-sided snapshot only).
scenarios: A new Blocks link created directly in Jira between two synced/active tickets, adopted inbound before either local ticket records it
